Great game, tons of mechanics to learn and perfect
Great game, is a great story generator,  has a small learning curve,
a wonderful game, well worth buying to support the devs,
Incredible game with tons of hours of fun, only complaint is the steep learning curve
there are two bugs that make it unplayable and wish I could refund the game over
Amazing sandbox world simulation type game. Each world and embark has incredible depth and endless potential for fascinating stories to discover and unfold.

Honestly the best game I've ever played. From the moment i figured out how to play which did take forever I was captivated. Defo not a game for everyone but if your looking for an ultra in depth base builder thats really so much more this is for you.

This is not a game for the casual gamer or the completionist. It is joyful chaos. deep and baffling. Unending, until it ends very suddenly in a completely unexpected way.
I have been playing dwarf fortress on and off for years and it remains one of my favourite games and has inspired many other games I enjoy (I'm looking at you rimworld) the attention to detail is immense and the stuff it throws at you will have you shouting at your dwarves and calling your other half in from another room to go 'HOW DID THOSE SHEEP GET UP ON THAT WALL AND STARVE TO DEATH?!' or 'WHY HAS A 4 YEAR OLD PUNCHED A HERBALIST TO DEATH?!' there's a lot of death. I hope you like building tombs.

It's amazing, as someone who has previously tried pretty hard to get into DF but failed due to some reasons, I think this is a big step up, at least in getting new players over the initial hurdles. Like building stairs, work orders etc.

The new UI and graphics are stunning. making for many wanted QOL changes.
Dig the new sound track. Only positive things for me.

Very impressive.

there's a lot of little stuff this game won't tell you that you'll have to run to tutorials for but at the same time that stands as a testament to the depth of this game and once it clicks you'll love it im hard glazing tarn

Going on Steam was the worst thing that ever happened to this game and it's development cycle.

edit: Yep. They're gameifying the hell out of it. All the cute idiosyncrasies that made this game a gem of emergent gameplay will be slowly polished away in favor of consistency and user experience.

a game i want to love, and in some parts i do, but wrapping your head around the detail the developers put into this masterpiece, i'd be lying if i said i knew even a quarter of the mechanics in this game, but if you want a proper, gritty, life simulator with world building and settlement development into managing a kingdom. This is it.

7/10, i wish i could understand and play this more.
Good game. Been playing for over a decade and the steam version is bringing together so many quality of life features.

The problem with games like Dwarf Fortress is that they lure me in with some basic mechanics and small victories only to reveal that I have reached the limit of my capabilities far before I've even scratched the surface. I just have to keep pushing forward for some inexplicable reason, muddling my way through work orders and supply chains until I reach a modicum of mid-game success, only to realize I ignored something like my ENTIRE military getting caught in a landslide 4 months prior to a giant invasion because I was so in the zone.
And the worst part is, I try again right after.

Its basically the granddaddy of city builders. a very comprehensive simulation of a fantasy city built and populated by neurotic little bearded drunkards. you're very likely to fail your first few attempts at building a fortress, but you can always start a new fortress in the same world and try to work up to a position where you can try to reclaim to failed forts, or just start a new world and go from there. this is a game that I truly think may never get finished simply because there can always be more done with it to deepen the simulation, in a good way.

+ Addictive gameplay
+ Feels free
+ Won Modern Art prize in an American Major Art Gallery
+ Most detailed game in existence
+ Now with eye tweaking graphics and better interface better suitable for newer generations
- the bugs still persist in certain areas

I can't recommend it for one simple reason:

There are more bugs in this game then dwarves in my Fortress.
Don't spend 30 euros for this version to not recommend it saying it's not worth the money when the game is totally free on Toady One's website.

Its good, so much to do. Real open sandbox, you can do whatever you want from the start. Not that you will know how to.

The chaos of my world can't touch this one :D

This is not a drill. This is one of the most complex games ever created. It's hard to call it a game when you start to understand it at a deeper level. This is a Fantasy World Generator/Simulator, which doesn't fit neatly into the box of many of its contemporaries that came after it. This is the game that inspired Minecraft. This is the game that inspired Infiniminer. All rivers flow from one source and this is that source. Are you looking for a fantasy war simulator where you take on huge sieges at your own base? This is that game. Are you looking to create a peaceful utopia where all the games races and peoples can come together to drink and be merry? This is that game. Are you looking for a game where the world you exist in has thousands of years of recorded, readable, discernible history that you can read from start to finish? This is that game. Each world you generate can be any of the above, or more. Want a fort designed around just selling musical instruments? Done. Want to focus a fort on living aboveground instead of underground, building on the surface a more human-style fortress with walls and gates and bridges? This. Is. That. Game.

Whether you enjoy this type of game or not, You cannot deny that this entire project is a work of art.

On the surface its just a silly game about Dwarves. But deep down its a beautiful work of art.

While I'm not exactly good at the game, I see the mastery that was put into it and I deeply appreciate what this game does.

Dwarf Fortress has been a game I have always wanted to play. The new GUI has made it so much more approachable and I can see why this game has inspired so many others. I keep losing track of time playing this game and can easily see it being one of my top played games soon.
Greed is good until it comes in the form of a giant cave spider or angry goblins, Dig deep and breath in that good cave dust.

im only about 15 hours in but this seemingly simple game just keeps adding more complexity by me exploring the buttons, i was attacked by goblins so i rush to defend with my 10 dwarf squad with half gear i slaughter them but then i notice i have 2 dwarfs unable to walk and unconscious... this leads to a 10 min pause and wiki then emergency hospital built... they died in the hospital due to dehydration but we almost made it >_< games definately got a life of its own!!

update... its been awhile.. over 200 hours and still entertaining
Technical, demanding, rewarding. it's a work of art in it's complexity, scope and execution. If someone is describing you and they say "they play Dwarf Fortress", it somehow says a lot about you.

It's quite interesting. Definitely download DFHack on steam if you want to play this, it adds a lot of minor tweaks by default which make the game much nicer to play, mainly UI stuff. Really the UI is lacking many simple things. Ah well. Other than that, the game is pretty much what it says on the tin. You are not omniscient so you can't easily see all the complexity that is there, but the gameplay is satisfying enough, I think.

However, there is a bug known as loyalty cascades, which while FUN is not very fun to deal with. Being able to effectively randomly lose a chunk of your population because someone punched someone else is not nice.
The OG colony sim, to call it a labor of love would be an understatement

I made a concentration camp for my dwarves after they refused to move a corpse to the dumpster (The solution was to enable a dumb secret option to move trash from outside tiles because a tile of grass grew under the corpse)

A work of art and dedication from a small team of people who just wanted to make the game they always wanted to play. No studios, no producers, no board of directors or shareholders, just passion and time. This game has been hugely influential on the colony sim genre, and has been available for free since it's inception (with donations accepted) and still is on their site. 

The only reason they went ahead and made a steam version (with graphics and full mouse support!) was because of health reasons and mounting medical bills, and I was happy to pay full price for this title to help them towards that end. This game will live on in legend and memory long past their time, and hopefully remain in active development with the community forever.

My militia captain was possessed by a ghost and forced to topple a statue in a temple. Despite having done nothing wrong, he was turned into a vampire. To prevent him sucking any of my dwarves dry, I imprisoned him in a dungeon above ground. He had a little 2x2 cell with fortifications around him. I left him a crossbow and ammo to shoot intruders if he felt like it. He didn't. Instead, when the fire-breathing titan showed up, he just stood there while it tried to breathe fire at him through the fortifications. This lasted about 6 game months until the fire finally got into the cell somehow and burned the poor militia captain alive (or maybe "un-alive" with him being a vampire). Perfect game.

Amazing world sim that feels somehow more fluid and enabling than Rimworld. You start off with a decent colonist (i. e. dwarf) count so that there is none of the sluggish starting phase as in the default 3 colonists setting of Rimworld.
Also the work tends to be more smoothly automated once you get to use work orders, you can automate most anything but still be flexible with one-time orders.
The fact that you have dozens of layers means you can expand quickly (albeit vertically) and will not run into space issues any time soon. (compared to Rimworld in a stony region)

For me it's definitely the better game (although I really like Rimworld) just for the bottomless freedom you have. The simple fact of quick expansion with a lot more characters means you are not constantly hamstrung / bottlenecked by bad traits, RNG luck on abilities etc.

However, with just some hours in I cannot yet say if there is sufficient 'external' motivation from enemies to make the game feel challenging. Where I am right now it's mostly about satisfying the needs of your dwarves. And in any case, you can always play with the settings when creating a new map and make it as difficult as you like.

I can fully recommend it.

Perhaps the singularly most enjoyable gaming experience I have had. While not an adrenaline pumper, the satisfaction from seeing plans come together over in-game years combined with tension filled slap dash emergency fixes to sudden calamities is addictive.

In depth dwarf fortress simulation with a ton of mechanics. A large group laid siege and I watched my 140 dwarf fortress cut down to 0, my last man was paralyzed and slowly died over the course of 5 weeks while being tormented by ghosts in an underground mushroom farm. Learned a lot and enjoyed it. I recommend it but you have to know what you're getting involved in with this game.

Editing review for 2024 steam awards. Yes, still absolutely recommend this masterpiece.

So I guess my dwarf kingdom took over a goblin outpost before my time, and those goblins totally bred out of control until our expedition of "dwarves" left the kingdom for gold and glory. Long story short these goblins had I guess convinced themselves they were dwarves, and me until our liason showed up from the "mountainhomes"

Ui is unintuitive and clunky. Clicking 10 times to build something isn't fun, build->workbench->farming->carpetner->select material. The game really incentivizes you to use keyboard shortcuts, because the alternative is painful.
Having to google, because I couldn't understand how to change the squad equipment. You need to open squad menu, then press some button without a text, then finally change the equipment when the game doesn't show you any hints or dwarf weapon skills.
The simplest actions which could be done in a single window require going through a couple of them.
Having no standards regarding good UX in a UI heavy game is a huge mistake.

Camera is awful, you can only move it by tiles, and I found no reason why they couldn't make it smooth like in any other top-down game.

The game has nice ambient, but that's it. Dwarfs working, mining, building etc. produce no sound, the game is really quite.

I get that it was an ASCII terminal game played with the keyboard and the devs spent most of their time designing the gameplay, but it's 2026 and the game isn't that cheap either.
Losing is fun, but the things I've described aren't.
If you want a similar experience just play Rimworld.

Played adventure mode. Tried to parley with a demon master in a dark goblin fortress. He bit down onto my skull and shook me until my head popped off like a cork in response to my greeting.

10/10

I've lost count of how many times I've tried to cancel military orders and instead disbanded all my military squads without confirmation. This game seriously needs more quality of life patches. That said, it's been my obsession for like 20 years, so I can't not recommend it.

I've been playing off and on since 2012, I couldn't even estimate my true playtime, I have separate folders for every version so this doesn't even represent my playtime for steam release, my Dwarf Fortress folder is 42 GB; I ALWAYS come back, I donated $20 before there was even talk of a steam release and I'll happily donate more, yet I still have no idea how to use minecarts. It's the king of emergent gameplay, you can never run out of things to do, you can only fail to think dwarfly enough.

There have been some serious late-game performance upgrades recently with Putnam now on the dev team, I think her addition was one of the best moves that Bay 12 could have made.

You NEED the wiki. DFHack is also a incredible piece of software crafted by many loving fans in the community since 2010, and I highly recommend checking it out.
If I had to choose only one game to play for the rest of my life, I'd probably choose Dwarf Fortress.

Hard as nails, but enjayable above all else.
Adventure mode is a great adition to the game.
Love the new improved pixel art style that was not in the original.
This game has a passionate team behind it. Ands gets better with each update.

Enjoy the game !

10/10 game, bravo Tarn Adams.

If you told me I could only play a single video game for the rest of my life this would be the game. The depth of its content and storytelling capacity is seemingly never ending, and the absolute star of a community and modding capabilities make me really, truly believe I could play this game till the end of time.

Tarn Adams needs to be preserved by storing his mind in an AI so he can develop this game for forever.
Shameless positive review boost. I've been playing this on and off since 2011. Was stoked when it came to Steam. Open to suggestions for my next mega project!

DF is a great game and I've been playing the free version for a long time. I decided to give this a try, and the UI needs a total overhaul. And this is comparing it to the barebones ascii UI version. That one evolved for ease of use and cohesion. This new UI has so many menus you have to go in and out of to do what you want, and it doesn't follow its old logic.
I don't want to play this unless the interface is fixed.

This is the culmination of 20 years of development, made exponentially more accessible to casual players. The most rich worldbuilding ever contained within a game, made available to a much wider audience. The game is well worth the price if you've been driven away by the complexity in the free version. Even if you prefer the original version, Tarn and Zack have put so much of themselves into creating this masterpiece that they deserve every penny from the steam release.

jesus christ what a masterpiece of a game this is. I played way too long before getting it on steam. and I think I can sink in hundreds of hours into it without getting bored the slightest. thank you for working on it, thank you for updating it, thank you for maintaining it. I love you developers

The same beautifully complex simulation with an exciting fresh coat of paint, new clicky mouse controls, an informative tutorial for both new and old players alike, and all the detailed play-by-play breakdowns of each brutally agonizing sliced left floating rib, every mercilessly dented right shin and, even the most harrowing of pulped hearts mutilated beyond recognition. So what are you waiting for? STRIKE THE EARTH!
You can play an adventurer and grab someone by the neck while pulling out all their teeth

Thousands of hours learning and enjoying this game. It's a wonderful simulation to peer into and immerse yourself in. I have nothing but positive words. It's complex, and no amount of hearing that over and over will properly express that, but it's worth it.

The biggest thing that got me going was following along with someone else playing and following what they do. The tutorial can only go so far. It's much easier to follow the actions of someone instead of being handed a textbook.

The UI and graphics have made the greatest simulation of our species completely accessible to even the lowliest of casuals.

It is a gift we do not deserve.
It's not as hard as I was told and from what I hear it's way easier than the original was but it's still a good game.

The ageless classic, the masterpiece that is regularly updated since 2004, and the inspiration for countless other masterpieces, including Minecraft and Caves of Qud !

Dwarf Fortress , and the brothers who still develop to this day, walked a millennium before others could run, and there's nothing more that can be said.

A game that I've shadow put a gorillion hours into but primarily the 40d version, and I have to say, this version is very good. DF's learning cure before was already quite exaggerated, and with this version, if you just look up a guide, or even less just someone playing the game itself, it's very easy to play and do well (and more importantly have fun in).

As a returning player I admittedly do get somewhat frustrated at a handful of changes, as it makes my intuition on how to play change dramatically from previous versions, but the more I play the more I get use to the changes and fin useful ways to use them in stead of how I use to do things, as well as usually finding many other QoL improvements that make this version much more worth playing over 40d.

No other example of this when we consider content, dynamics and depth of it. Craziest game ever made as procedural-generation matter and depth at the same time. But of it's sake it still has things need to fixed like bugs, glitches and some "working wrong" or "not working" mechanics etc. and improved (you still need DfHack to improve QoL and many bugfixes for example.).. And i really hope this game will be fixed and improved in future even more...

I got into this game finally after having it in my library for two years, and I decided to start up a tutorial world and follow the game's instructions to the best of my ability. After completing the tutorial, I suddenly had a problem: the staircase that led into my base wasn't being used because I had mined a hole into the side of the hill where my fort resided. I had also laid flooring on top of the staircase, believing that the flooring would not affect the staircase (the flooring, in fact, deleted the staircase).

I then foolishly blocked off the side hole and attempted to rebuild the staircase to no avail (bug, possibly?). My dwarves had no way to leave, and they began to die of dehydration. I thought quickly to order a dig so that they would get water, but I had ordered the mass mining of all the lower elevations below a few minutes ago, and I didn't think to cancel the order as I watched all 18 of my dwarves die. A series of mistakes had left to the greatest stupid wipe in the history of Dwarf Fortress. 

10/10, perhaps the greatest game ever created.

tldr.text: Very Positive (95%): players praise the graphics and gameplay, while bugs and crashes are the main complaint.
Some reviewers also find the learning curve steep.

details.text: Recent reviews are slightly less positive than the all-time score, a gap of 3 points.
Players with under 2 hours are a little less positive than those with over 50 hours, and some point to the "steep learning curve" as the early hurdle.
